# Fix or Refund? — Full EU Consumer Rights Reference (2026)

Canonical URL: https://fixorrefund.shop/
Languages: English (en), Greek (el)
Privacy: 100% client-side local calculation; zero user inputs transmitted to servers.
Disclaimer: Independent informational guide, not a government service or qualified legal advice.

## 1. Directive (EU) 2019/771 (Sale of Goods — Statutory Legal Guarantee)
- Minimum 2-year legal guarantee of conformity from delivery against the professional seller across all 27 EU Member States.
- The seller—not the manufacturer—is legally liable. Commercial warranties cannot shorten or replace statutory rights.
- Reversed burden of proof: at least 12 months EU-wide. Member States may extend this to 24 months.
- Member States may set longer guarantee periods. This site shows the EU minimum only and has not verified national rules; it does not state country-specific periods.
- Second-hand goods: may be reduced by agreement, never below 1 year.
- Remedies hierarchy: Free repair or free replacement first; proportionate price reduction or full refund (contract termination) if impossible, disproportionate, refused, delayed unreasonably, repair fails, or defect is severe.

## 2. Directive (EU) 2024/1799 (EU Right to Repair — Applicable from 31 July 2026)
- +12-month legal guarantee extension (once) when the consumer chooses repair over replacement for sales contracts from 31 July 2026 in transposed Member States.
- 5–10 year post-warranty manufacturer repair obligation at reasonable price and time for Annex II product categories:
  Smartphones, slate tablets, cordless phones, TVs/electronic displays, washing machines/washer-dryers, dishwashers, fridges/freezers, tumble dryers, vacuum cleaners, domestic local space heaters, welding equipment, servers/data-storage equipment, and light-transport battery devices (e-bikes/e-scooters).
- Anti-repair barriers prohibited: compatible, second-hand, or 3D-printed spare parts allowed; no refusal based on prior independent repair.

## 3. Directive (EU) 2024/825 (Harmonised Notice & GARAN Label — From 27 September 2026)
- Mandatory EU harmonised legal guarantee notice in-store and online.
- Official GARAN label for products offering a free whole-product producer durability guarantee exceeding 2 years.
